::: {.kicker}
Baghdád · 1862
:::

::: {.lead}
The Kitáb-i-Íqán was revealed by Bahá'u'lláh in the space of two days and two nights, in answer to
four questions put to Him by one of the maternal uncles of the Báb. Over fourteen sessions we read
it from beginning to end.
:::

> In fact, all the Scriptures and the mysteries thereof are condensed into this brief account. So
> much so, that were a person to ponder it a while in his heart, he would discover from all that
> hath been said the mysteries of the Words of God, and would apprehend the meaning of whatever
> hath been manifested by that ideal King.
>
> [Bahá'u'lláh]{.attrib}

## Why this Book

> The Íqán is the most important book written on the spiritual significance of the Cause. I do not
> believe any person can consider himself well versed in the teachings unless he has studied it
> thoroughly.
>
> [Shoghi Effendi]{.attrib}

Bahá'u'lláh gives the key-note here and explains some of the outstanding passages of the Sacred
Books — in the hope, as Shoghi Effendi put it, that the friends will *continue to study the Sacred
Books by themselves and unfold the mysteries found therein.* That is the point of this study: not
to be handed conclusions, but to leave with the tools and the confidence to read the Writings on
your own.

## Goals of the study

1. To develop the tools and confidence to read the Writings by yourself.
2. To advance in our understanding of core Bahá'í beliefs and worldview, and how to explain them to others.
3. To appreciate the significance of the Íqán, and how it can inform our service and our life in general.
